name: vulkan-prf-swapchain
title: Vulkan stage F: window surface, swapchain and present (blit of the offscreen frame), out-of-date/suboptimal recreate, resize and minimise, present modes, GPU selection API; pure choice functions unit-tested on every leg, headless-surface swapchain tests on lavapipe, the real window verified on the user's GPU PC (issue #43, stage F)
issue:
Approved by the user 2026-10-14 with ALL recommended choices (proposal with the user's decisions: C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/vulkan-backend.md; read it FULLY first: section 2 contract ('Render target and readback': Vulkan ALWAYS renders into its own offscreen colour+depth image and, with a window, Present blits it to the swapchain image, so CI exercises everything a window uses except the final blit/present; 'Headless': Initialize(nullptr, w, h) with no surface and no swapchain extensions; 'Colour space': UNORM target everywhere, the lit shader encodes in-shader when linear), section 3 ('swapchain present + resize/minimise, validation clean, Shutdown destroys everything'), section 5 row 'F Window, swapchain, present' ('Surface, swapchain (fixed format choice), blit offscreen -> swapchain, out-of-date/suboptimal recreate, minimise (0x0), present mode, wireframe, GPU selection API, docs (application/text/ui/meshes pages)'; CI proves 'compile + unit tests of format/extent/present-mode choice only'; needs the user's GPU), section 7 risks (lavapipe hides real-driver issues), section 9 'Cannot be verified without hardware' (swapchain creation, surface format/colour-space choice, present modes (mailbox/FIFO, vsync), resize/minimise/out-of-date handling, HiDPI framebuffer sizes, real-window input, discrete-vs-integrated scoring with two GPUs, vendor quirks, validation-clean on a real driver, performance) and 'Decisions (user, 2026-10-14)': always render offscreen and Present copies to the window; OpenGL stays the default renderer until THIS stage passes on the user's real GPU (and even then changing the default is a separate decision, optional G: NOT in this PR); the editor host keeps refusing --renderer vulkan in v1). WHAT EXISTS (read the real files): renderer/include/renderer/vulkan/VulkanRenderer.hpp + renderer/src/vulkan/VulkanRenderer.cpp (stage 0 core; VulkanDraw.cpp/.hpp draws, VulkanResources.cpp/.hpp meshes/textures, VMA in VulkanMemoryAllocator.cpp/VulkanVma.hpp). Initialize(GLFWwindow* windowHandle, w, h) does `static_cast<void>(windowHandle); // no surface yet` and runs CreateInstance -> SetupDebugMessenger -> PickPhysicalDevice -> CreateLogicalDevice -> CreateAllocator -> CreateCommandPool -> CreateFrameResources -> CreateRenderPass -> CreateDrawResources -> CreateTargets; any failure calls ShutdownLocked and keeps InitStatus {NotInitialized, Ok, NoVulkanRuntime, NoSuitableDevice, ValidationUnavailable, Failed} + GetInitMessage; a second Initialize shuts down first and calls EndLifetime() (the lifetime token every resource holder checks). CreateInstance: apiVersion VK_API_VERSION_1_1; instance extensions are ONLY VK_EXT_debug_utils and only with validation (WantsValidation: N2_VULKAN_VALIDATION=1/0, ValidationMode Default/Enabled/Disabled, Debug builds on when the layer is installed); no surface extensions. PickPhysicalDevice: enumerates devices, needs apiVersion >= 1.1, the FIRST queue family with VK_QUEUE_GRAPHICS_BIT (_graphicsFamily), ColorFormat R8G8B8A8_UNORM with COLOR_ATTACHMENT|TRANSFER_SRC|TRANSFER_DST optimal features, a depth format (FindDepthFormat); scores by ScoreDeviceType (discrete 1000, integrated 500, virtual 200, CPU 100, other 10), highest wins, first on ties; NoSuitableDevice otherwise. CreateLogicalDevice: ONE queue from _graphicsFamily (_graphicsQueue), device extensions only VK_KHR_portability_subset when offered, features only fillModeNonSolid when supported (wireframeSupported; SetWireframe before Initialize handled). Frames: MAX_FRAMES_IN_FLIGHT = 2, FrameResources {commandBuffer, fence}; BeginFrame waits the slot fence (FenceTimeoutNanoseconds 10 s; failure sets _deviceLost and logs), FlushRetired(slot), begins the command buffer and the render pass on the offscreen _framebuffer, sets a NEGATIVE-height viewport (GL y-up) and scissor, BeginDrawFrame; EndFrame ends the pass, EndDrawFrame, resets the fence and vkQueueSubmit with it (no semaphores), advances _currentFrame. The colour image rests in VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL between frames (render pass initialLayout UNDEFINED with a clear, finalLayout TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL, comment: 'read back, and blitted to a swapchain (stage F)'); because the y flip is in the viewport, image row 0 is the TOP of the picture (ReadFramebuffer flips rows to bottom-first), so a blit to a swapchain image needs NO flip. ReadFramebuffer copies with SubmitOneTime (vkQueueWaitIdle) and resamples nearest for another size. Present() today: logs ONCE per renderer (guarded by _warnedWindow) 'Vulkan renderer: Vulkan swapchain/present is not implemented yet (stage F): frames render offscreen and the window stays blank' and does nothing. Resize(w,h) ignores 0x0 ('a minimised window'), stores _requestedWidth/Height and recreates the offscreen targets (RecreateTargets: AbandonOpenFrame, vkDeviceWaitIdle, DestroyTargets, CreateTargets) unless _targetFixed; OnResize(int,int) forwards positive sizes to Resize; SetRenderTargetSize fixes the size (_targetFixed) for the editor viewport. GetCompatibleGPUs/SelectGPU(VkPhysicalDevice)/GetRecommendedGPU(gpus) are public stubs ('stage F') returning {}/false/VK_NULL_HANDLE; struct GPUInfo {device, name, type, vramMB, vendorId, isSupported, driverVersion, apiVersion, limits} exists. ShutdownLocked: vkDeviceWaitIdle, DestroyDrawResources, DestroyAllResources, DestroyTargets, render pass, fences, command pool, DestroyAllocator, vkDestroyDevice, debug messenger, vkDestroyInstance; then resets every member. VulkanRenderer.hpp includes <vulkan/vulkan.h> BEFORE <GLFW/glfw3.h> (after Renderer.hpp, which pulls glad first), so GLFW's Vulkan functions (glfwVulkanSupported, glfwGetRequiredInstanceExtensions, glfwCreateWindowSurface, glfwGetFramebufferSize) are declared. renderer/include/renderer/common/RendererConfig.hpp: N2ENGINE_RENDERER_VULKAN (CMake option, default ON; the GCC 14 CI leg builds it OFF, so every new Vulkan file and every engine/lua_project change must compile with it OFF). Backend selection today: Config::ApplicationOptions::renderBackend (engine/include/engine/config/ApplicationOptions.hpp: OPENGL, VULKAN, SOFTWARE) passed to Application::Init; the Application::Init() default is OPENGL; lua_project/src/Main.cpp parses '--renderer opengl|software' ONLY (default software; vulkan is rejected as unknown); the editor host refuses --renderer vulkan (editor-server/src/Host.cpp ToRenderBackend, tests/editor-server/HostOptionsTests.cpp ~171-181): KEEP that refusal. Docs: docs/application.html '#vulkan-renderer' (the stage list, the 'Device', 'Target' and per-method bullets, the callout '#design-vulkan-offscreen' 'a window (stage F) will get a blit of the finished colour image at Present'); docs/gpu-particles-checklist.html (the model for the new checklist page: nav sidebar, h1 with a PR badge, a lead paragraph, a 'Hardware rule' callout, sections Requirements / 1. Revert / What to report, footer; listed in docs/README.md's page table and linked from its feature page); docs/testing.html '#vulkan-tests' and the GPU smoke-test section (lua_project --renderer opengl). OpenGL's Present is just glfwSwapBuffers (no swap interval is set anywhere: the driver default, normally vsync on), and OpenGL with a fixed SetRenderTargetSize renders into an FBO and does not show it on the window.

SCOPE (all inside renderer/src/vulkan/ and renderer/include/renderer/vulkan/ unless stated; IRenderer UNCHANGED; the headless path Initialize(nullptr, ...) must stay byte-for-byte in behaviour: no surface, no surface/swapchain extensions, same device choice as today when no preference is given):
(1) SURFACE: when windowHandle != nullptr, CreateInstance also enables the instance extensions glfwGetRequiredInstanceExtensions returns (VK_KHR_surface + the platform one; check glfwVulkanSupported() first and fail with a clear InitStatus/message if GLFW cannot reach a Vulkan loader or returns no extensions, e.g. a new InitStatus value such as NoSurface or Failed with the reason: decide, document); after the instance (and messenger), create the VkSurfaceKHR from the renderer's OWN instance with glfwCreateWindowSurface(_instance, window, nullptr, &_surface) (the surface must come from this instance; the engine never creates one); destroy it in ShutdownLocked after the device and before vkDestroyInstance. Initialize on a window whose GLFW context API is not GLFW_NO_API fails cleanly (glfwCreateWindowSurface returns VK_ERROR_NATIVE_WINDOW_IN_USE_KHR): log the reason. Keep the window handle only for glfwGetFramebufferSize (and nothing else; no GLFW callbacks are installed by the renderer: resize comes through OnResize).
(2) DEVICE AND QUEUES: with a surface, a device qualifies only if it also offers VK_KHR_swapchain, has at least one surface format and one present mode for the surface, and has a queue family with presentation support (vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceSupportKHR). Prefer ONE family with both graphics and present (the norm on desktop); if a device has only separate families, either support it (a second queue, the swapchain in VK_SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT or a queue-family ownership transfer of the swapchain image) or skip that device with a log: choose, document. Enable VK_KHR_swapchain only with a surface. The headless path keeps today's first-graphics-family rule.
(3) GPU SELECTION API (public VulkanRenderer methods, IRenderer unchanged): make the device choice a PURE function over plain candidate descriptions (e.g. renderer/include/renderer/vulkan/VulkanDeviceChoice.hpp, Vulkan types allowed but no device calls: candidate {index in enumeration order, name, type, apiVersion, deviceLocalBytes, hasGraphics, formatsOk, presentOk (or 'not needed'), swapchainExtOk} + a GpuPreference {none | index | case-insensitive name substring}) returning the chosen index and the reason. DEFAULT (documented): the highest-scoring qualifying device by type (discrete > integrated > virtual > CPU > other, as ScoreDeviceType), ties broken by more device-local memory, then enumeration order. A preference that names a qualifying device wins; one that names nothing or a device that does not qualify logs ONE warning naming the preference and the device used instead, and falls back to the default (never a failure). Sources of the preference: a SetGpuPreference(...) call before Initialize (name it to fit), else the environment variable N2_VULKAN_GPU (an integer = index, anything else = name substring; read with the existing GetEnvironment helper). Implement GetCompatibleGPUs() (after Initialize: every enumerated device with GPUInfo filled, isSupported = qualifies for THIS renderer's surface or headless needs, in enumeration order; empty before Initialize), GetRecommendedGPU(gpus) (the pure default rule over GPUInfo), and SelectGPU(device): the engine never switches device mid-run, so define it safely (recommended: before Initialize it is not usable (no instance) and returns false; after Initialize it returns true if `device` is the current one, else false with one log line pointing to SetGpuPreference + Initialize again; or implement a full re-initialise if you can keep every caller's resources' lifetime-token semantics: choose, document in the header). Add GetDeviceName/GetDeviceType (exist) to the log line at Initialize: 'Vulkan renderer: using <name> (<type>), chosen by <default|preference ...>'. lavapipe in CI must still be chosen (it is the only device; N2_VULKAN_EXPECT_CPU_DEVICE=1 checks it).
(4) SWAPCHAIN (fixed, documented choices; each a PURE function in e.g. renderer/include/renderer/vulkan/VulkanSwapchainChoice.hpp over plain structs (VkSurfaceCapabilitiesKHR, std::vector<VkSurfaceFormatKHR>, std::vector<VkPresentModeKHR>, the framebuffer size, a vsync flag), so every rule is unit-tested without a device): ChooseSurfaceFormat: the offscreen image is R8G8B8A8_UNORM and already holds the final ENCODED bytes (gamma lighting writes them as they are; linear lighting encodes in the lit shader since stage C; unlit/text/UI are identical in both spaces), so the swapchain must take those bytes UNCHANGED: prefer B8G8R8A8_UNORM + VK_COLOR_SPACE_SRGB_NONLINEAR_KHR, then R8G8B8A8_UNORM + SRGB_NONLINEAR, then any other 8-bit UNORM format with SRGB_NONLINEAR (A8B8G8R8_UNORM_PACK32); a single VK_FORMAT_UNDEFINED entry means 'any' -> B8G8R8A8_UNORM; NEVER pick an *_SRGB swapchain format while a UNORM one exists (a blit into an sRGB image would encode the already-encoded bytes a second time: everything too bright); if ONLY sRGB formats exist, pick the first one and log ONCE that colours will be double-encoded (or render the present through a UNORM view with VK_KHR_swapchain_mutable_format if offered: optional, document which); never index an empty list (return a 'no format' result, Initialize/recreate fails cleanly). Explain the choice in a design callout (why not sRGB; how this matches OpenGL's on-screen bytes: GL's default framebuffer is sRGB-capable and only the lit linear path writes through GL_FRAMEBUFFER_SRGB, so on both backends the window shows encoded bytes). ChoosePresentMode(modes, vsync): vsync on (DEFAULT) -> FIFO (always available per spec, and the safe fallback for any list); vsync off -> MAILBOX if offered, else IMMEDIATE if offered, else FIFO; expose vsync as a VulkanRenderer method (e.g. SetVSync(bool), effective at the next swapchain recreate) plus the environment variable N2_VULKAN_VSYNC=0/1 for the checklist (no IRenderer or engine API change; OpenGL sets no swap interval, so the engine has no vsync option today: say so in the docs). ChooseExtent(caps, framebufferW, framebufferH): caps.currentExtent when its width is not 0xFFFFFFFF, else the framebuffer size clamped to [minImageExtent, maxImageExtent] per axis; a 0 in either axis (currentExtent 0x0 or framebuffer 0x0: minimised) is reported as 'minimised', never clamped up to 1. ChooseImageCount(caps): minImageCount + 1, clamped to maxImageCount when maxImageCount != 0. Also pure helpers for the decisions below (IsMinimised, the recreate decision: given the last acquire/present VkResult, a pending-resize flag and the current vs swapchain extent, return {present normally, recreate then present next frame, skip (minimised), device lost, surface lost}). Swapchain creation: imageUsage TRANSFER_DST (check caps.supportedUsageFlags; and the chosen format's optimal features include BLIT_DST, else fall back to a vkCmdCopyImage path only when the format and size match exactly, else log once and skip presenting: decide, document), preTransform = currentTransform, compositeAlpha OPAQUE if supported else the first supported bit, clipped TRUE, oldSwapchain = the previous one on recreate (destroy the old one after the new one exists and nothing uses it).
(5) PRESENT: keep the always-offscreen design. EndFrame keeps submitting the frame exactly as now (ReadFramebuffer and the headless path must not change). Present(), with a swapchain: if no frame was submitted since the last Present, or the swapchain is minimised/absent, do nothing (no warning); else vkAcquireNextImageKHR with a per-frame-in-flight image-available semaphore, record into a per-slot present command buffer (or extend the frame's own submission if you restructure EndFrame: then prove ReadFramebuffer and the headless tests unchanged): barrier the offscreen colour (stays in TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL; make the frame's colour writes visible to the transfer read) and the swapchain image (UNDEFINED -> TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL), vkCmdBlitImage the whole offscreen image to the whole swapchain image (VK_FILTER_NEAREST when the sizes match, VK_FILTER_LINEAR when they differ and the source format supports SAMPLED_IMAGE_FILTER_LINEAR, else NEAREST; stretch to fill, no letterbox: document; the R/B channel order difference is handled by the blit's format conversion), then swapchain image -> PRESENT_SRC_KHR; submit waiting on image-available at TRANSFER stage and signalling a render-finished semaphore that is PER SWAPCHAIN IMAGE (the current validation layer flags a present-wait semaphore reused per frame slot: VUID-vkQueueSubmit-pSignalSemaphores-00067), with a fence so the slot's next BeginFrame also waits for the blit before reusing its command buffers and semaphores; the NEXT frame's render pass writes the offscreen colour again, so its external dependency must also order after the blit's transfer READ (write-after-read): check the render pass's srcStageMask/srcAccessMask (TRANSFER) cover it; vkQueuePresentKHR on the present queue. When the window has a fixed render size (Window::SetRenderSize -> SetRenderTargetSize, the editor viewport), the offscreen stays at that size and the swapchain follows the window: the blit scales (OpenGL shows nothing in that case: list it as a documented difference, not a bug).
(6) RECREATE, RESIZE, MINIMISE, LOSS: VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR from acquire -> recreate the swapchain (when not minimised) and skip this present; VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR from acquire -> present this frame, recreate before the next; OUT_OF_DATE or SUBOPTIMAL from present -> recreate before the next present. OnResize/Resize (the existing path; OnResize gets 0x0 when minimised) marks the swapchain for recreation and still resizes the offscreen target when not fixed (0x0 changes nothing of the offscreen target, as today); recreate waits only for what uses the old swapchain (vkDeviceWaitIdle is acceptable: document), re-queries the surface capabilities, uses ChooseExtent; minimised (extent 0x0) -> no swapchain recreation and no present until a non-zero extent returns, frames still render offscreen (BeginFrame/EndFrame unchanged, ReadFramebuffer still works), no busy error spam (at most one log line per minimise, preferably none). VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST anywhere in acquire/submit/present -> _deviceLost = true with one log line (the existing 'frames are skipped' behaviour; Shutdown still cleans up). VK_ERROR_SURFACE_LOST_KHR -> recreate the surface and swapchain once; if that fails, stop presenting with one log line (frames keep rendering offscreen). Remove the 'swapchain/present is not implemented yet (stage F)' warning and _warnedWindow (Present on a headless renderer is a silent no-op, as the software renderer's headless Present). Shutdown: wait idle, destroy present command buffers (with the pool), semaphores, fences, the swapchain, then (after the device) the surface; validation reports nothing. Re-Initialize with the same window must work (the old surface is destroyed with the old instance before the new one is created: GLFW allows one surface per window at a time).
(7) WIREFRAME: SetWireframe works on the windowed path exactly as offscreen (no change expected; the checklist verifies it on screen if the demo has a toggle; else a Vulkan-only test already covers it offscreen).
(8) ENGINE/DEMO (minimal, compile-safe with N2ENGINE_RENDERER_VULKAN OFF): lua_project/src/Main.cpp accepts '--renderer vulkan' (RenderBackend::VULKAN; title 'Vulkan'; the usage text 'opengl|vulkan|software'; with Vulkan compiled out it still parses and Window's existing FailInit message explains); the default stays software for lua_project and OPENGL for Application::Init(); Window.cpp/Window.hpp change ONLY if something is needed (e.g. a clearer FailInit message from GetInitMessage of a VulkanRenderer); NO change to the editor host (it keeps refusing --renderer vulkan), ApplicationOptions, the protocol, or any default.

CI-VERIFIABLE TESTS (renderer_tests; new files under tests/renderer/vulkan/, inside the N2ENGINE_RENDERER_VULKAN guard in tests/renderer/CMakeLists.txt): (a) DEVICE-FREE, plain TESTs run on EVERY Vulkan-ON leg (both Windows legs, both Linux Clang legs): VulkanSwapchainChoiceTests.cpp with tables of fake capability structs: ChooseSurfaceFormat (B8G8R8A8_UNORM preferred over R8G8B8A8_UNORM, UNORM over SRGB in any order, the single UNDEFINED entry, only-sRGB lists (the documented fallback + flag), the wrong colour space, an empty list -> none, never out-of-range); ChoosePresentMode (vsync on -> FIFO whatever is offered; off -> MAILBOX, else IMMEDIATE, else FIFO; empty/odd lists -> FIFO); ChooseExtent (a defined currentExtent wins even if the framebuffer differs; currentExtent 0xFFFFFFFF -> framebuffer size clamped to min/max per axis, incl. below-min and above-max on each axis separately; 0x0 currentExtent and 0xN framebuffer -> minimised; HiDPI framebuffer sizes larger than the window's); ChooseImageCount (min+1; maxImageCount 0 = unbounded; min == max; min+1 > max); the minimise detector; the recreate-decision table (SUCCESS, SUBOPTIMAL from acquire and from present, OUT_OF_DATE from acquire and from present, pending resize, minimised, DEVICE_LOST, SURFACE_LOST). VulkanDeviceChoiceTests.cpp: the pure device choice over fake candidates (discrete over integrated over CPU; ties by memory then order; a device without present support or VK_KHR_swapchain is excluded with a surface and allowed headless; index and name-substring preferences, case-insensitive; an out-of-range index or unknown name falls back to the default and reports the reason; a preference naming a non-qualifying device falls back; the N2_VULKAN_GPU parse (integer vs name, empty)). (b) LAVAPIPE (device tests on the VulkanTest fixture: validation ON, zero errors AND warnings, no leaks; they EXECUTE in both Linux Clang legs with N2_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1 and N2_VULKAN_EXPECT_CPU_DEVICE=1, skip on Windows without a device, compiled out on GCC 14): GPU selection on the real instance (GetCompatibleGPUs lists lavapipe as supported after Initialize, GetRecommendedGPU picks it, SelectGPU semantics as documented, N2_VULKAN_GPU/SetGpuPreference naming lavapipe by name and by index chooses it and naming nonsense falls back with ONE warning; the headless path's choice is unchanged); the headless renderer's Present is now a silent no-op (no warning; replace any earlier test that asserted the 'not implemented yet' warning: the ONLY earlier assertion that may change). HEADLESS-SURFACE SWAPCHAIN TESTS (VulkanHeadlessSwapchainTests.cpp): Mesa's WSI offers VK_EXT_headless_surface on lavapipe in recent Mesa [M: check on the CI image, ubuntu-24.04 Mesa]; behind a capability check, add a TEST-ONLY way to run the real swapchain path without a window (e.g. a SetHeadlessSurfaceForTest(width, height) before Initialize(nullptr, ...) that enables VK_KHR_surface + VK_EXT_headless_surface and creates the surface with vkCreateHeadlessSurfaceEXT; its currentExtent is undefined (0xFFFFFFFF), so the 'framebuffer size' comes from a test-settable size instead of glfwGetFramebufferSize: the same seam lets the test simulate resize and minimise (0x0)), and test: swapchain creation with the documented format/present mode/image count; many frames of BeginFrame/draw/EndFrame/Present (more than 2x MAX_FRAMES_IN_FLIGHT and more than the image count) validation-clean; resize via OnResize -> recreate at the new extent (and the offscreen target follows); a fixed SetRenderTargetSize with a different 'window' size presents (scaled blit) validation-clean; minimise (0x0) -> Present skips, no recreate, frames still read back; restore -> recreate and present again; forced OUT_OF_DATE and SUBOPTIMAL (a test hook that makes the next acquire/present report them) -> the documented recreate behaviour; vsync off -> MAILBOX/IMMEDIATE/FIFO per what lavapipe offers; re-Initialize and Shutdown with a swapchain leak nothing. Content check where possible: the swapchain images cannot be read back through the public API, so add a test hook that copies the last presented swapchain image to the host (or skip the content check and say so in `unverified`); if added, the presented pixels equal ReadFramebuffer's (row order and R/B order right) for an unscaled present. N2_REQUIRE_VULKAN DECISION for this extension: these tests GTEST_SKIP with a clear reason ('VK_EXT_headless_surface not offered by this driver: the swapchain path was not executed') when the extension is missing EVEN under N2_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1 (skip-with-warning: the extension is optional and not part of the driver contract the other tests rely on); add an opt-in N2_REQUIRE_VULKAN_HEADLESS_SURFACE=1 that turns that skip into a failure, and if the CI log shows lavapipe offers the extension on BOTH Linux Clang legs, set that variable for those legs in .github/workflows/tests.yml so the swapchain tests cannot silently stop running; report in the PR body which legs executed them (and if the extension is missing on the CI image, say so and list the whole swapchain path under `unverified`). Every existing test keeps passing unchanged (except the one Present-warning assertion above, if any); do not weaken any stage 0/A-E assertion; the GCC 14 (Vulkan OFF) leg must build lua_project and the engine.
